messages:
maria: Hey @eng-sre — customer acme.ai seeing intermittent 502s hitting /v1/generate around 2026-03-15T14:22:00Z. They supplied request_id `r_0a3f7b9c` and said response body had "upstream reset". Can someone look up server logs for that req_id?
eli: Can you paste their curl or full request headers + exact timestamp window? Need the client-side X-Request-Id if present. Also, did they hit hosted or dedicated?
maria: They hit hosted (us-west). Customer provided this curl (redacted token):
```
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-medium","input":"hello"}'
```
They saw a 502 and the response header included `x-request-id: r_0a3f7b9c`. They reported the event at 2026-03-15T14:22:01Z.
jamie: Quick note on retention: edge/ingress access logs are kept for 14 days, request-level application traces (jsonPayload) are retained for 30 days. So this one is still within retention.
alex: Searching tips — try both the structured field and free-text. Example searches:
Kibana Lucene: `request_id.keyword:\"r_0a3f7b9c\" OR message:*r_0a3f7b9c*`
gcloud (if needed):
```
gcloud logging read 'jsonPayload.request_id="r_0a3f7b9c"' --project=redwood-prod --limit=50 --freshness=1d
```
Or grep rotated logs: `zgrep -n "r_0a3f7b9c" /var/log/redwood/*/*.gz`
Also check the gateway component logs and the runtime worker logs in the same time window (+/- 30s). Which exact 60s window should I scan?
maria: Please search 2026-03-15T14:21:30Z to 2026-03-15T14:23:00Z. Customer can also run the curl with `-v` and send the raw output. They said this happened twice in ~2 minutes.
alex: Found entry in runtime-worker-3 at 2026-03-15T14:22:01.856Z — snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:22:01.856Z] ERROR request_id=r_0a3f7b9c upstream connection reset by peer while proxying to backend instance i-0f9d3a (kv_cache=hit)
```
Full trace shows `TCP_RST` from backend within same second. Pushing to runtime oncall — looks like an upstream process crash or socket limit.
sam: I have the instance. I'll pull system logs + dmesg for that time window and check OOM / segfault. If we confirm crash I'll remove it from pool and rotate.
maria: Thanks — I'll update the customer with provisional cause (backend reset) and ask them to provide `-v` curl output and whether they were sending large inputs. Please post final root cause here once confirmed. :thumbsup:
